steps.text: All physical quantities are built from seven SI base units: kg, m, s, A, K, mol, cd.
Every equation must be dimensionally homogeneous: both sides have the same units.
Derived units, e.g. newton = kg m s⁻², follow from defining equations.
Scalars (mass, energy, time) have magnitude only; vectors (force, velocity) have magnitude and direction.
Vectors add tip-to-tail; perpendicular components add with Pythagoras.
Check: s = ut + ½at² gives m = (m/s)·s + (m/s²)·s² = m. ✓
